source: The region of Inner London-West is an outlier: its GDP is more than 600% of the EU average and, consequently, receives little in EU catch-up funds.
claim: Inner London - West (UKI3) tops the regional GDP index at 626, far above the next highest regions, Luxembourg (253) and Southern Ireland (220).

source: regions containing the country’s capital ⦿ are much more developed than others.
claim: The 28 regions containing a country capital average 135.8 on the regional GDP index, against 91.2 for the other 253 regions.

source: There are also islands of development in regions containing country capitals
claim: In Spain, France, the UK, Poland, Romania and Slovakia the capital region scores well above its country on the GDP index: Madrid 124 vs 92, Paris 177 vs 104, London 168 vs 106, Warsaw 152 vs 70, Bucharest 144 vs 63 and Bratislava 179 vs 76.

source: Notice the sub-country divisions: Italy (developed north, less developed south), Belgium (the same) and Germany (developed west, less developed east).
claim: Northern Italian regions average 117.3 on the GDP index against 66.4 in the south (central Italy 97.0); Flemish Belgium averages 116.8 against 88.6 in Wallonia (Brussels 196.0); western Germany averages 126.3 against 93.0 in the east.

source: The capital, Budapest, was lifting the surrounding area of Pest out of the "less developed region" category (< 75% EU average GDP).
claim: Budapest's regional GDP index is 139 while the surrounding Pest region's is 53.

source: Lithuania’s capital, Vilnius, is economically the most developed part of the country and is lifting the country’s GDP over the 75% threshold, jeopardizing the catch-up funds that would be allocated toward the less developed areas of the country.
claim: Lithuania's capital region (Sostinės regionas) scores 112 on the GDP index against 65 for the rest of the country (Vidurio ir vakarų Lietuvos regionas).

source: Poland has done the same with its capital, Warsaw, which has now also been separated into its own region.
claim: Warsaw's region (Warszawski stołeczny, PL91) scores 152 on the GDP index against 59 for the surrounding Mazowiecki regionalny (PL92).

source: The range of regional economic development is quite high for many countries
claim: Within-country spreads of the regional GDP index are wide: the UK's regions run from 65 to 626, Romania's from 39 to 144, France's from 34 to 177, Germany's from 83 to 202 and Italy's from 58 to 143.
